proposed_change.summary: The object registry has no object representing the backend/API surface, so half of TIB-5460's oracle has nowhere to live. Propose extending the taxonomy with a backend/API object (or an explicit decision that API knowledge stays attached to portal/storefront objects, with a documented rule for endpoints that have no such parent).
proposed_change.proposed_object_key: api (name to be decided by qa-context-lifecycle-orchestrator)
proposed_change.rationale: _registry.json lists exactly 9 objects (artwork, asset-category, campaign, font, global-option, order, product-base, sdk, translation) and every one is a portal/storefront business object. No object_key carries an API or backend alias. TIB-5460's server-side halves - the thumbmark issuance endpoint GET /merchant/{platform}/thumbmark and the per-visitor+per-product quota counter - fall outside the model entirely. The structural symptom is already visible in canon: the thumbmark endpoint ended up in payload.unmapped_evidence in TWO separate objects (sdk and translation) precisely because there is nowhere to model an endpoint with no portal/storefront capability attached to it. This is a taxonomy gap, not a staleness problem: a fresh Flow 1 run would hit the same wall.
proposed_change.scope_note: This is a registry/taxonomy decision, not a TIB-5460 decision. Raised here because the task exposed it, not because the task should drive it.
